correct_completion: I would buy a house by the sea.
full_sentence: If I won the lottery, I would buy a house by the sea.
acceptable_variants: I would travel around the world.
I would give some money to my family.

options.text: I bought a house by the sea yesterday.
options.why_wrong: The past simple describes a real past event, but the second conditional needs 'would' for an unreal, imagined situation.

options.text: I would buy a house by the sea.
I will buy a house by the sea.
options.why_wrong: The future form 'will' is used for real possibilities; the second conditional with 'if' and a past verb describes an unlikely situation.

options.text: I buy a house by the sea every year.
options.why_wrong: The present simple describes a habit, not an imagined result of winning the lottery.

grammar_focus: Second conditional for imagined present or future situations
explanation: The second conditional uses a past simple verb in the if clause and would plus the base verb in the main clause. Learners often mix up the tenses of the two clauses.
translation: Se eu ganhasse na loteria, eu compraria uma casa à beira-mar.
